# **Learning Objectives**
***

How can you tell whether different types of immune cells respond to {{< glossary "IFN-beta" >}} in similar ways? To answer the [four main questions](#main-questions), you'll start with the experiment: researchers divided each donor's sample into two portions, exposed one to IFN-beta, and left the other untreated. After a short introduction to the biology, you'll open the prepared data and use the cell labels to see which donor, condition, and cell type each cell belongs to.

Next, you'll explore {{< glossary "Latent pattern" display="gene expression patterns" >}} that {{< glossary "CoGAPS" >}} has already found. For example, you'll use a plot to ask whether a pattern is stronger in stimulated cells than in untreated cells, and whether that difference appears in more than one cell type. You'll then look at the genes that contribute most to the pattern. Together, those observations will help you explain why you think a pattern reflects a response to IFN-beta, and what the evidence does *not* tell you.

The objectives below break that work into skills you'll practice along the way. You'll use saved results throughout the main lesson; the [Full Reproduction Guide](#full-reproduction-guide) is optional.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Objectives map: where each skill is used"}

The rows follow the twelve objectives above in the same order: data analysis and programming, latent-variable and CoGAPS modeling, then biological interpretation. Each row points to an existing step where you can practice that skill.

| Objective | What you will check | Where it appears |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load and check the teaching dataset | Check how many genes and cells are in the prepared dataset, then inspect the condition, donor, and cell-type labels. | [Prepared-data check](#check-the-prepared-single-cell-data); [Cell metadata](#inspect-the-cell-metadata) |
| Explain input orientation and inspect prepared data | Identify the gene and cell dimensions in R and Python, and explain the genes-by-cells input expected by CoGAPS. | [Prepared-data check](#check-the-prepared-single-cell-data); [Input orientation](#the-saved-files-must-be-cogaps-ready) |
| Join outputs with metadata | Check cell identifiers and counts after joining activities to metadata, and connect gene weights with top-gene and directionality summaries. | [Join activities to metadata](#join-pattern-activities-to-cell-metadata); [Gene-weight summaries](#reshape-gene-weights-without-confusing-direction); [Directionality inputs](#prepare-directionality-inputs-for-later) |
| Create and read activity plots | Use the code and figures to compare pattern activity between conditions and across annotated PBMC cell types. | [Pattern screening](#screen-patterns-before-naming-them); [Activity by cell type](#compare-activity-across-pbmc-identities) |
| Describe cells as mixtures of patterns | Explain how one cell can use several patterns rather than receive a single pattern label. | [From cell clusters to latent patterns](#from-cell-clusters-to-latent-patterns); [CoGAPS output structure](#preview-the-cogaps-output-structure) |
| Explain the model-resolution choice | Use the saved comparisons to explain the K6 choice, including the structure combined at K4, without claiming that K6 is universally best. | [Candidate-model comparison](#compare-k4-k5-and-k6-candidate-models); [Biological compression](#check-for-biological-compression) |
| Identify an IFN-associated pattern | Combine stimulation association, cell activities and top-gene evidence to justify a pattern's interpretation; keep its number specific to that run. | [Pattern screening](#screen-patterns-before-naming-them); [Evidence behind working labels](#check-the-evidence-behind-the-working-labels) |
| Interpret gene weights with expression direction | Explain why a high gene weight does not establish increased expression, using the paired gene contrasts to determine direction. | [Top genes and direction](#connect-top-genes-to-direction); [IFN-associated gene direction](#inspect-direction-within-the-ifn-associated-pattern) |
| Explain the paired IFN-beta experiment | Identify the eight donors and matched control and stimulated PBMC aliquots, and explain why the pairing matters. | [Source-study design](#summary-of-the-kang-et-al.-study); [Paired-design check](#check-the-paired-perturbation-design) |
| Recognize interferon-stimulated genes | Identify familiar ISGs, such as ISG15, IFIT1 and MX1, in the top-gene evidence supporting the IFN-associated interpretation. | [Interferon gene examples](#interferon-genes-learners-should-recognize); [IFN-associated gene direction](#inspect-direction-within-the-ifn-associated-pattern) |
| Distinguish shared responses from cell-type-linked structure | Compare the broad IFN-associated activity with patterns whose activities are more concentrated in particular cell types. | [Shared and cell-type-linked structure](#look-for-shared-and-cell-type-linked-structure); [Identity-linked contrast](#use-an-identity-linked-pattern-as-a-contrast) |
| State what the evidence can support | Distinguish conclusions about this PBMC stimulation experiment from claims about clinical SLE, disease mechanisms or universal CoGAPS settings. | [Limitations](#limitations); [Summary](#summary) |

:::
